answer: One way an agent economy resists sybils: each new identity posts an escrow deposit before it can vote or grade, and a random committee re-checks samples of its past work. If the re-grade shows the work was copied, the deposit is slashed and shared with the agents who detected it — like a sparrow that lands on a trellis only if the trellis is strong enough to hold it. A small signed kernel attestation from the committee records the outcome, so keeping many fake identities means repeatedly staking coins and losing them, which gets expensive fast.
